questions.q: Standard thickness of glass shower door
questions.n: 10mm (or 3/8 inch) is the industry standard thickness for frameless tempered glass shower doors, providing a balance of strength and weight.

questions.q: The most economical roofing
questions.n: Corrugated G.I. sheets are the most cost-effective roofing material due to low material cost and simple installation.

questions.q: What is the MOST efficient slope % for pipes that serves water to the Residential Building
questions.n: A 2% slope (1/4 inch per foot) is the standard and most efficient slope for residential sanitary drainage to ensure proper flow velocity.

questions.q: Most economical spacing of purlin
questions.n: 0.60 meters (600mm) is considered the most economical spacing that still provides adequate support for standard gauge roofing sheets.

questions.q: Vertical reinforcement of CHB wall
questions.n: As per Max Fajardo's references, 0.80 meters is the typical maximum vertical reinforcement spacing for standard CHB wall construction.

questions.q: A type of beam with a thickened support/base?
questions.n: A haunched beam has a deeper section at the supports to resist high negative moments and shear forces.

questions.q: Engineered wood is purchased per?
questions.n: Engineered wood products like laminated flooring or panels are typically sold by the square meter.

questions.q: Not part of a structural plan?
questions.n: The Site Development Plan (SDP) is part of the Architectural or Civil documents, not the Structural structural engineering set.

questions.q: Another term for I beam
questions.n: Wide Flange (W) beams are the most common type of I-shaped structural steel member.

questions.q: What glass not to use in interior
questions.n: Low-Emissivity glass is designed to reflect thermal radiation and is meant for the building envelope; using it inside offers no energy benefit and is unnecessarily expensive.

questions.q: Which is not a type of HSS
questions.n: This is a non-standard acronym, likely a distractor for HSS (Hollow Structural Section).

questions.q: In preparation of formworks for concrete pouring, which is/are needed?
questions.n: Phenolic-coated plywood is specifically designed for formwork because of its smooth surface and water resistance.

questions.q: Thinner used in latex paints?
questions.n: Latex paints are water-based (aqueous), meaning they are thinned and cleaned up with water.

questions.q: Foundation to be used for weak soil
questions.n: A mat or raft foundation distributes the building load over the entire footprint, making it ideal for low-bearing capacity (weak) soil.

questions.q: Shallow foundation
questions.n: Isolated footings are the most common type of shallow foundation.

questions.q: Column with poured concrete inside
questions.n: A Lally column is a structural steel pipe filled with concrete to increase its load-bearing capacity and fire resistance.

questions.q: What is placed in between two different roof slopes
questions.n: The valley gutter is the internal intersection of two roof slopes where water collects and drains.

questions.q: Where should shear wall be located?
questions.n: Shear walls are most commonly located at the central core (elevator and stairs) to provide lateral stability to the building.

questions.q: minimum size of aggregates to be used sa bedding
questions.n: 25mm (roughly 1 inch) is a standard minimum for aggregate bedding under slabs or pipes to ensure stability and drainage.

questions.q: not a standard thk of Chb
questions.n: Standard CHB comes in 4", 6", and 8" thicknesses; 10" is not a common commercial size.

questions.q: when to remove formworks and shores for beams
questions.n: Soffit forms and shores for beams (spans up to 6m) typically require 14 days for the concrete to gain enough strength to be self-supporting.

questions.q: recommended/minimum slope of roof
questions.n: A slope of 12 to 15 degrees is the typical minimum recommended for standard corrugated or rib-type metal roofing to ensure effective water runoff.

questions.q: ratio of plaster/mortar?
questions.n: The standard ratio for plastering and mortar (Class A) is 1 part cement to 3 parts sand.

questions.q: compressive strength for slab on grade?
questions.n: 3000 psi is the standard compressive strength for residential slabs-on-grade and general reinforced concrete.

questions.q: compressive strength for columns?
questions.n: The standard design strength for columns in low-to-medium rise buildings.

questions.q: exterior wall facing (identify through description)
questions.n: Wood Plastic Composite (WPC) panels are commonly used for exterior cladding due to their weather resistance and wood-like appearance.

questions.q: Which has a built in P-trap?
questions.n: A water closet (toilet) has an integral S-trap or P-trap as part of its ceramic molding.

questions.q: What is the meaning of VOCS?
questions.n: VOCs are chemicals that evaporate at room temperature and are a major concern in paint and building material indoor air quality.

questions.q: sandwich exterior wall facing
questions.n: Aluminum Composite Panel (ACP) consists of a core material sandwiched between two thin aluminum sheets.

questions.q: determines the stregth of concrete
questions.n: The water-cement ratio is the most critical factor; lower ratios yield higher strength concrete.

questions.q: A ________ certificate is a quality assurance document used in the metals industry
questions.n: A Mill Certificate (or Mill Test Report) verifies the chemical and physical properties of steel.

questions.q: Best glass to use in sky lights
questions.n: Laminated glass is best for skylights because if it breaks, the interlayer holds the fragments together, preventing them from falling.

questions.q: white deposits on walls that hard to solve
questions.n: Efflorescence is the migration of salt to the surface of a porous material (like concrete or masonry), forming a white coating.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a regulating valve?
questions.n: Gate valves are intended for fully open or fully closed service; they are not used to regulate or throttle flow.

questions.q: Which of the following valves is best used for water containing solid wastes
questions.n: Butterfly valves have a simple disc and a straight-through flow path that handles slurry or waste better than other types.

questions.q: Linear Valve used for regulating water flow
questions.n: The globe valve uses a linear motion (up/down) of the disc to regulate flow volume precisely.

questions.q: Which glass is used for banks
questions.n: Laminated glass (multi-layered) is used in banks for bullet resistance and security against forced entry.

questions.q: Which area is more complicated for construction
questions.n: Steep slopes require complex grading, retaining walls, and difficult access for equipment and materials.

questions.q: who should issue Cert. of Electrical Inspection
questions.n: Official certificates of inspection (CEI) are issued by the Office of the Building Official (OBO) via city hall inspectors.

questions.q: Best door to counter the air heat coming from outside going inwards the bldg
questions.n: A revolving door acts as an airlock, maintaining the interior temperature even while people enter and exit.
